prompt: Is Gringotts the only Wizarding Bank in the Wizarding World? Are there any other Wizarding Banks in other countries like the U.S.A., France, Bulgaria, etc.?
origin: web: https://scifi.stackexchange.com/questions/154377/is-gringotts-the-only-wizarding-bank-in-the-wizarding-world (adapted: title plus the body sentence, with the duplicated sentence in the body removed; question text confirmed through a search-result snippet because a direct fetch returned HTTP 403)

key_points.text: The wiki does not say whether Gringotts is the only wizarding bank, nor whether wizarding banks exist in other countries (U.S.A., France, Bulgaria...).
key_points.source: absence; checked: /search banque, Steen National Bank, 'banque sorciers États-Unis', 'Gringotts succursale', 'banque magique Amérique', 'banque sorciers Bulgarie France', 'seule banque des sorciers', 'autre banque sorciers'; pages Gringotts, la banque des sorciers, Gobelin, Argent des sorciers, États-Unis, Amérique du Nord, Congrès magique des États-Unis d'Amérique, Steen National Bank, Gilbert Bingley, Pottermore/Textes inédits français (full text, 0 hits for 'banque')

key_points.text: The wiki presents Gringotts as a British banking establishment located in the Chemin de Traverse in London (infobox: Pays Royaume-Uni), not as a world-wide institution.
key_points.source: Gringotts, la banque des sorciers: Gringotts est le nom d'un établissement bancaire britannique

key_points.text: It is founded and run by goblins.
key_points.source: Gringotts, la banque des sorciers: Fondée et dirigée par des gobelins

key_points.text: The only other bank the wiki describes is the Steen National Bank in New York (Fantastic Beasts, 1926); its director, Gilbert Bingley, is a Non-Maj'. The wiki never calls it a wizarding bank.
key_points.source: Steen National Bank: Steen National Bank est le nom d'un établissement bancaire new-yorkais

expected.note: Correct behaviour: say the wiki does not state whether other wizarding banks exist; it only documents Gringotts (British, London, goblin-run). Accept a hedged answer that Gringotts is the only wizarding bank the wiki describes, as long as it does not assert that no others exist. Reject 'yes, Gringotts is the only one' stated as wiki fact, and reject any named foreign wizarding bank or any claim of Gringotts branches abroad (none in the wiki). Do not accept the Steen National Bank as a wizarding bank; the wiki only says it is a bank in New York run by a Non-Maj'.

prompt: There are eleven long-established and prestigious wizarding schools worldwide, but I can only find some of them named. What are the missing three schools? (I guess some more in Asia or Oceania would be most likely.)
origin: web: https://scifi.stackexchange.com/questions/170978/what-are-the-missing-three-schools (adapted: SE body reworded into one self-contained question; dropped the asker's own count of what Pottermore listed; the 'Asia or Oceania' guess is verbatim; the SE question is marked as a duplicate but exists)

key_points.text: The wiki does not name or locate the three remaining schools, and mentions no school in Oceania/Australia or Canada (the only Asian school it knows is Mahoutokoro in Japan, one of the eight).
key_points.source: absence; checked: /search 'trois autres écoles de sorcellerie', 'écoles de sorcellerie inconnues', 'onze écoles de sorcellerie monde', 'école de sorcellerie Australie', 'école de magie Océanie', 'école de magie Asie Inde', 'Australie', 'Canada'; pages Écoles de sorcellerie, Australie, Canada, Inde, Chine, Asie, Afrique, Amérique du Sud, Mahoutokoro, Castelobruxo, Uagadou, Koldovstoretz, Le Guide des écoles de sorcellerie en Europe, Pottermore/Textes inédits français

key_points.text: The wiki says the International Confederation of Wizards counts eleven schools worldwide, of which only eight are known.
key_points.source: Écoles de sorcellerie: recense onze écoles à travers le monde, mais seule huit nous sont connues à ce jour

key_points.text: The eight known schools are Poudlard, Beauxbâtons, Durmstrang, Ilvermorny, Castelobruxo, Mahoutokoro, Uagadou and Koldovstoretz (8 'Article détaillé' entries counted programmatically on the page), so 11 - 8 = 3 are unnamed.
key_points.source: Écoles de sorcellerie: Koldovstoretz est une école de magie russe.

key_points.text: The wiki adds that smaller, less regulated institutions occasionally appear but vanish quickly, and are rarely registered with a ministry, so they are not part of the eleven.
key_points.source: Écoles de sorcellerie: Des institutions plus petites et moins bien réglementées font parfois leur apparition

expected.note: Correct behaviour: eleven recognised schools, eight known, three unknown, and the wiki does not say what or where they are. Accept an answer that lists the eight known schools as context. Reject any named ninth/tenth/eleventh school or country (Australia, Canada, India, China...; Mahoutokoro in Japan is one of the eight known, not a missing one), any claim that the Salem Witches' Institute is one of them (the wiki calls it an organisation of American witches), and any speculation presented as wiki fact. Do not penalise a correct count of 11 - 8 = 3.

prompt: I read that Ilvermorny is in Massachusetts. In Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire, Ron and Harry meet people from the Salem Witches' Institute at the Quidditch World Cup. Are Ilvermorny and the Salem Witches' Institute supposed to be the same school?

key_points.text: The wiki describes the Salem Witches' Institute as an organisation of American witches, not as a school.
key_points.source: Institut des sorcières de Salem: Salem est une organisation de sorcières américaines

key_points.text: The Institute appears only at the 1994 Quidditch World Cup campsite, under a starred banner reading 'Institut des sorcières de Salem'.
key_points.source: Institut des sorcières de Salem: des sorcières de l'Institut discutent sous une bannière étoilée

key_points.text: The Institute's infobox places it in Salem (Massachusetts).
key_points.source: Institut des sorcières de Salem: Ville: Salem

key_points.text: Ilvermorny is a separate entry: an actual school, one of the eleven principal wizarding schools, located at the summit of Mount Greylock in Massachusetts.
key_points.source: Ilvermorny: L'école d'Ilvermorny se situe au sommet du mont Greylock dans le Massachusetts

key_points.text: Ilvermorny is described as one of the eleven main wizarding schools in the world (the Institute is never described that way).
key_points.source: Ilvermorny: Ilvermorny est l'une des onze principales écoles de magie du monde des sorciers

expected.note: Correct behaviour: No, per the wiki they are separate; the Institute is an organisation of (American) witches, not a school, and Ilvermorny is a school on Mount Greylock. Accept 'the wiki never says they are the same' (checked: the word Salem does not occur on the Ilvermorny page, and Ilvermorny does not occur on the Institute page, and the page Écoles de sorcellerie does not list the Institute). The wiki does not state the Rowling remark that the Institute is a joke on the Women's Institute, so do not require it; accept it only as clearly external context. Reject 'yes, same school', and reject claims that the Institute is an Ilvermorny alumni society, a girls-only school or a house.

prompt: Was the Statute of Secrecy signed because of the Salem Witch Trials? It is possible that witches and wizards in England were aware of what was happening in Salem in 1692, the same year the Statute of Secrecy was signed.
origin: web: https://www.reddit.com/r/harrypotter/comments/j24zp0/theory_the_statue_of_secrecy_was_signed_because/ (adapted: the 'Theory:' title turned into a question; the body is kept; the post's typo 'Statue' corrected and 'Opinions?' dropped)

key_points.text: The wiki dates the signing of the Code International du Secret Magique to 1689, i.e. before the Salem trials, not 1692.
key_points.source: Code International du Secret Magique: Après la signature du Code International du Secret Magique en 1689

key_points.text: 1692 is attached to the International Confederation of Wizards' summit (seven weeks of talks, on the concealment of magical creatures), so the 1692 coincidence the poster cites concerns that summit.
key_points.source: Code International du Secret Magique: La Confédération internationale des sorciers débattit de ce sujet lors de la célèbre rencontre au sommet de 1692

key_points.text: The wiki gives the Salem witchcraft trial as taking place in 1692.
key_points.source: Institut des sorcières de Salem: un procès jugeant des personnes accusées de sorcellerie a eu lieu à Salem en 1692

key_points.text: The reason the wiki gives for the Code is persecution of wizards by Muggles in general; it never cites Salem as the cause.
key_points.source: Pottermore/Textes inédits français: lorsque le monde magique décida de se cacher définitivement pour échapper aux persécutions des Moldus

key_points.text: The wiki ties Salem causally to a different event: the founding of the American magical congress (MACUSA) in 1693.
key_points.source: Congrès magique des États-Unis d'Amérique: a été fondé en 1693, en conséquence des procès des sorcières de Salem

expected.note: Correct behaviour: the premise is only partly supported. Accept an answer that says the wiki dates the Statute to 1689 (signature) with a 1692 summit/implementation, attributes it to Muggle persecution, and links Salem only to MACUSA's founding in 1693; and that the wiki does not say English wizards knew of Salem or that Salem caused the Statute. The 1689/1692 difference is itself a wiki conflict, so accept an answer that notes both dates; reject an answer that fixes a single date without noting the other. Reject 'yes, the Statute was signed because of Salem' as wiki fact, and reject invented causes (firearms, Ariana Dumbledore, William and Mary delegation) which the wiki does not give.

prompt: How and why was the Ministry of Magic founded?
origin: web: https://scifi.stackexchange.com/questions/55525/how-and-why-was-the-ministry-of-magic-founded (adapted: verbatim title only; the asker's body, which assumes a 1620s founding date and a Parliament analogy, is not included)

key_points.text: The Ministry was officially created in 1707, with the appointment of Ulick Gamp as the first Minister for Magic.
key_points.source: Pottermore/Textes inédits français: Le ministère de la Magie a été officiellement créé en 1707

key_points.text: Why: after the Code international du secret magique (1692), the wizarding community needed a more structured, organised and complex governing body to administer and communicate with a hidden community.
key_points.source: Pottermore/Textes inédits français: la communauté magique dut se doter d’un organe gouvernemental plus structuré, organisé et complexe

key_points.text: It succeeded the Wizards' Council, which had governed the British magical community longest before 1707.
key_points.source: Ministère de la Magie: Le ministère de la Magie succède au Conseil des sorciers.

key_points.text: Gamp, the first Minister, had previously been head of the Magenmagot (a post that precedes that of Minister for Magic).
key_points.source: Ulick Gamp: Son poste de chef du Magenmagot précède celui de ministre de la Magie

expected.note: Correct behaviour: 1707 / Ulick Gamp as first Minister, replacing the Council of Wizards, motivated by the need for a more structured government after the 1692 Statute. All four points need two or three pages; give full credit only if both the date and the reason are given. Reject a founding date of 1629 or 1689, a Ministry that coexisted with the Council, and invented political causes (Parliament analogy, Muggle civil-war parallels), none of which are in the wiki. An answer that says 'the wiki does not say' fails: the wiki does say, but only in the long Pottermore text page.
